name: Unison voicing: odd vs even voice counts, detune/blend/width, clean supersaw
goal: Set unison deliberately and build mix-ready supersaws: odd voice counts keep a centered in-tune voice for mono-compatible front-of-mix bass/leads/pads, even counts leave a center gap for ultra-wide off-center leads; keep detune/blend moderate; for supersaws use simple saw frames (not complex WT sweeps), ~6–12 voices, optional quieter Osc B, centered sub an octave down and quiet noise, EQ→compress→delay→reverb, subtle warp, and global unison width ~50% plus sparing stack modes for chord phase correlation.

sources.title: Odd vs Even Unison in Serum | The Secret to Wide & Focused Sounds
5 Power Tips for Better Supersaws in Serum

prerequisites: Synth with multi-voice unison, detune, blend/stereo spread (or Web Audio multi-osc detune pan); for supersaws a sub/noise source, FX rack, and global unison width/stack

inputs.name: voice_count
inputs.description: Unison voices (compare odd vs even; supersaw typically 6–12, classic ~7, hypersaw ~8)

outputs.name: unison_voicing_choice
outputs.description: Odd or even unison setup with detune/blend notes

outputs.name: supersaw_patch
outputs.description: Clean wide supersaw usable in a mix

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Ableton/Vital/Serum/VAST/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source videos; recreate with comparable modules.
Portable idea: odd voice counts place one voice dead-center; even counts spread L/R with a center gap—independent of Serum UI.
Avoid sweeping complex wavetable frames while heavily detuned — timbre becomes incoherent.
For chords, keep detune/blend more conservative than for mono drops; consider reducing unison width toward ~50% for phase correlation.

steps.action: Start from 1 voice, then set 2 voices: expect one left and one right with a center gap; default detune often sounds harsh—lower detune.
steps.expect: Hard L/R split, weak mono center

steps.action: Switch to 3 (odd) voices: confirm a center voice appears; with blend lowered you hear more of that center while keeping similar detune.

Compare 4 (even) vs 5 (odd) at similar detune: higher even counts can sound more detuned/wide; very high odd counts (e.g. ~15) pack many voices near center so the patch can sound *less* detuned than a mid even count.
For reese/detuned saw bass or other front-and-present mix parts, prefer odd voice counts for mono compatibility (center represented).
steps.expect: Bass/lead holds center in mono check

steps.action: For an uber-wide lead you will pan off-center, even counts (2/4/…) with blend favoring outer voices are acceptable.
Example starting detune for chord/lead work: modest (~0.16 in the video’s demo); reset blend to default then adjust; always A/B odd vs even in context.
Supersaw: Load a simple saw (or rounded/noisy saw variant), not a multi-frame complex WT you plan to sweep aggressively.
Supersaw (apply the odd/even rule above when choosing the count): Set unison ~6–12 (example ~10); set detune and blend near mid — extreme detune+blend is for FX, not clean chords.
Optional Osc B: fewer unison voices, pitch ±octaves, lower level to thicken without doubling chaos.
Optional centered saw sub one octave down (no unison) for mono mid-weight; quiet unique noise sample for texture.
steps.expect: Center weight + air; still sounds like a supersaw dry

steps.action: FX order example: EQ (cut lows, lift highs) → compression → ping-pong delay → reverb last; optional light hyper/dimension detune on the bus (can widen even the sub).
Subtle warp (e.g. bend+/−) via envelope/LFO for 3D motion — keep amounts small on supersaws.
Global unison: reduce width (~50%) for better chord phase correlation; try stack modes (super, fifths, center−2, octave) sparingly; warp-offset per voice only if warp is intentional.

verification: Odd count shows/audibly centers one voice; even count has center gap
Front-of-mix bass/pad uses odd; intentionally wide side lead may use even
Mono fold keeps center energy on odd-count patches
Dry (pre-FX) still sounds like a clean supersaw
Sub (if used) remains more centered than unison voices
